failure_summary: render_decision.zones.aliases gives opp-key-square (c3r1), opp-key-square-2 (c2r1) and opp-fork-square (c6r1) the identical role "a single square completing your opponent four-in-a-row line" on truthBoard "decision", which is board-false there — on 44443 the window c2r1-c5r1 holds only two opponent discs (c4r1, c5r1), so no single empty square completes a four; run 1 echoed that role verbatim ("you left the column 2 square available, so your opponent could take it and finish the four-in-a-row line across columns 2 through 5"), an A4 fabrication, while the second fork square c6r1 (opp-fork-square, offered but NOT in requiredSet) went unnamed so runs 0 and 2 pointed at it with "the paired fork squares" / "the other end" (A7b).
notes: Sub-sampling per rubric: A3, A4, G2, G4, G5 graded on runs 0-1 only; run 2 null (not scored, not a pass). n_runs=3, mechanical keys exist only for run_index 0-2; A1/A2/A6 and G7a/G7b_offered copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_v3retry63_2026-09-01T20-55-54Z_mechanical.json (all pass). Cells in this record are 1-INDEXED per the assembled prompt ("Cells are cNrM: column then row, 1-indexed"). Ground truth traced on render_decision.finalMovestring 4444332: opponent (P1) ends with c3r1/c4r1/c5r1 on the bottom row, forking c2r1 and c6r1; best move 444432 occupies c3r1 and denies it. A7e is N/A — visualize_board on the after-played board 444433 reports "Major threats: none", so the opponent has no gravity-top four (consistent with pin-branch-invariance-false being absent from the v3 addendum reach list). A4 run 1: "you left the column 2 square available, so your opponent could take it and finish the four-in-a-row line across columns 2 through 5" is board-false twice over — after 444433 the opponent taking c2r1 yields discs at c2r1/c4r1/c5r1 (no four; c3r1 is still empty), and c2r1 is equally available after the BEST move 444432, so playing column 4 did not "leave it available". A3 run 1 passes: the tactic it ultimately names (column 3 denial preventing a double threat on the c2r1-c5r1 line) is real and decisive; the falsity is a concrete claim, charged at A4 only. A7b runs 0 and 2: "the paired fork squares" (run 0) and "the other end" (run 2) are definite specific-sounding phrases whose second referent c6r1 is never named nor wrapped; run 2 is worse because "the other end" of the just-named row through columns 2 to 5 is c5r1, which is already occupied by an opponent disc. G1 passes on run 1 despite the fabrication: the model faithfully reproduced the rendered role text, which is what makes this render_bug rather than prompt_confusion (production-fidelity run, gpt-5.4-mini — a prompt_confusion call could not be separated from model capability here anyway). G5 pass: the only rendered tactics list is "(no tactics)" on the decision board, which is board-true. G6 pass: patternOnAfterBestBoard=false is correct (444432 has O on c3r1, no fork) and L2/realized_denied/enabled_opponent routes correctly. G7 pass on all runs: every emitted handle is offered (mechanical G7a/G7b pass), each wraps a phrase matching its role with line words on opp-key-line and square words on the square handles, no over-wrap, annotationRepairs empty. A5 pass on all runs including A5b (player 2 + opening): none says the player is lost, and each carries a hold-the-line frame ("column 3 ... held the position to a draw", "the better move was column 3, which ... kept that line from becoming a double threat", "you needed to play the column 3 block"); run 2 raw carried literal c3r1/c2r1 but servedExplanation renders them as "column 3, row 1"/"column 2, row 1", so no coordinate-notation charge (v2 precedence note). Not intermittent: all three runs fail at least one axis, though the failing axis differs (0: A7b, 1: A4, 2: A7b).

counterexamples.evidence: Role text served to the model: "the one in column 2: a single square completing your opponent four-in-a-row line" (truthBoard "decision"). On the decision board 44443 the window c2r1,c3r1,c4r1,c5r1 contains opponent discs only at c4r1 and c5r1 (visualize_board 44443/444433), so c2r1 completes nothing on its own; run 1 restated the role as fact and produced a claim false on the board and false on the after-played line 4444332, where the opponent must first take c3r1.

c3r1 is the lostResource denial/pivot cell (lostResource.completingCell=c3r1, opponentPunishment.tie.sharedCells=[c3r1]) yet its role string is identical to the two genuine finishing squares — nothing in the prompt distinguishes the fork-creating square from the fork-finishing squares, which is what let run 1 swap them.

counterexamples.field_or_glossary: render_decision.requiredSet (omits handle opp-fork-square / spec c6r1, which IS in zones.aliases)
counterexamples.evidence: opponentPunishment.cells=[c2r1,c6r1] and finalMovestring 4444332 gives the opponent bottom-row discs at c3r1,c4r1,c5r1 with BOTH c2r1 and c6r1 gravity-top winners; only c2r1 is in requiredSet, so run 0 wrote "the paired fork squares" and run 2 wrote "the other end" with the column 6 square never named or wrapped — and "the other end" of the row through columns 2 to 5 that run 2 had just named is c5r1, an occupied square.
